details:
Developed by Team Aero Engineers, the "Space Radiation Defense" project is an autonomous deep-space shielding framework designed to protect astronauts from lethal radiation during lunar and Mars missions without adding heavy launch mass penalties.

The Project Challenge & Solution

Operating outside Earth's geomagnetic field exposes crews to severe radiation hazards, specifically Solar Particle Events (SPE), Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR), and trapped radiation within the Van Allen Belts. To solve this, the project introduces a comprehensive, three-pillar defense architecture:

  • Pillar 01: Detection & Early Warning – Utilizes real-time active cabin dosimetry (silicon detectors and TEPC), passive crew tracking, and deep-space heliophysics sensors to provide a 15 to 60-minute early warning lead time before solar proton storms arrive.
  • Pillar 02: Mitigation & Shielding – Employs a multi-layer graded-Z hull architecture that integrates light-weight aluminum structural bumpers with hydrogen-rich materials like High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and water. These low-Z materials effectively slow down heavy ions and block radiation without generating dangerous secondary X-ray cascades. Surface options also incorporate local regolith and wearable AstroRad vests.
  • Pillar 03: Survival & Storm Shelter – Features a central core refuge inside the habitat that can be rapidly assembled within 60 minutes during a solar storm. This shelter achieves a zero mass penalty by utilizing dual-use mission consumables—such as water storage jackets, food rations, and supply racks—to surround and protect the crew, cutting acute solar storm dosage by over 50%.
